_id_ranges: CaseMasterID 9001-9019 | AccusedMasterID 8001-8053 | VictimMasterID 7001-7020 | ComplainantID 6001-6020 | Employee/Unit/Court IDs come from lookups.json

_code_conventions.OccupationID: 1=Business/Shop Owner, 2=Farmer, 3=Government Employee, 4=Private Employee, 5=Driver, 6=Homemaker, 7=Student, 8=Daily Wage Worker, 9=Self-employed/Professional, 10=Retired (no OccupationMaster table yet - see DATA_STORE_SCHEMA.md Extended tables)
_code_conventions.ReligionID_CasteID: 0 = Not specified for all records in this dataset - CasteMaster/ReligionMaster tables aren't built (deferred, see DATA_STORE_SCHEMA.md), and we deliberately don't assign specific values to fictional people for a demo dataset
_code_conventions.cross_entity_ids: Evidence records (calls/transactions/cctv/witnessStatements/timeline) cite people by a scenario-local narrative token 'P1','P2',... = 1st, 2nd, ... distinct accused of that scenario. Each scenario's 'personIndex' resolves those tokens to the GLOBAL Accused.PersonID ('KA-Pnnnn'), which is unique and stable across the whole dataset - the same human keeps one ID across every FIR and scenario. 'personRefs' is the human-readable glossary of the same tokens; non-person tokens (e.g. C1 'V4' a SIM, C9 'W1' a witness) appear only there. Vehicle/account/phone refs remain scenario-local strings.

cases.title: The Yeshwanthpur Fencing Ring
cases.summary: A motorcycle theft ring in Bengaluru launders stolen bikes through fake registration transfers sold as 'used vehicles' in Tumakuru. One accused (Suresh) is named inconsistently across the two FIRs - the entity-fusion target. CCTV places him in Tumakuru at a time his own witness statement says he was elsewhere in Bengaluru.
cases.assignmentReason: Vehicle theft and forged transfers - ordinary property crime. Spans two districts, but Bengaluru City and Tumakuru SPs coordinate directly; no CID trigger.

firs.BriefFacts: Complainant reports 3 motorcycles stolen from a paid parking lot near Yeshwanthpur station between 8:15-8:30pm.
4 buyers report being sold motorcycles with forged registration transfer papers by a man identifying himself as a used-vehicle dealer.

personRefs.P1: Suresh Naik / Suresh N. (AccusedMasterID 8001 & 8003 - SAME PERSON, entity-fusion target)
personRefs.V4: unregistered SIM used only to coordinate the ring, traced to Iqbal

calls.note: First contact, a week before the theft

transactions.note: 2 days after the Tumakuru sales
Same session as TX-1

cctv.note: On the Bengaluru-Tumakuru highway, ~90 min drive to Tumakuru sale site

witnessStatements.statementText: Saw two young men near the bikes around 8pm, one on a phone call the whole time.
I was at my sister's house in Rajajinagar, Bengaluru, from 7pm to 11pm on 19 March. I was nowhere near Tumakuru.

timeline.description: Suresh's vehicle on NH-48 toward Tumakuru
Forged-papers vehicle sales in Tumakuru (incident date)
Iqbal pays Suresh's account, 2 days post-sale

contradiction.description: Suresh's alibi (WS-2: in Bengaluru until 11pm on 19 March) directly conflicts with CCTV placing his vehicle on the Tumakuru highway at 9:40pm the same night - a ~90min drive that makes both being-in-Bengaluru-until-11pm AND being-on-the-highway-at-9:40pm mutually exclusive.
contradiction.suggestedNextQuestion: Ask Suresh to account for his vehicle's presence on NH-48 at 9:40pm on 19 March, given his statement places him in Rajajinagar until 11pm the same night.

transactions.note: Cash withdrawal same day as pawn shop gold melt-down entry

I run a licensed pawn shop. I have never dealt with Praveen Achari.

timeline.description: Praveen enters Ravindra's pawnshop with a bag

personRefs.P1: Zoya Merchant / Z. Merchant (AccusedMasterID 8009 & 8011 - SAME PERSON, entity-fusion target, registers under two front company names)
personRefs.P2: Tarun Bhatia (AccusedMasterID 8010 & 8012, call-centre lead, same name both FIRs but worth confirming same person)

calls.note: Same recurring pattern, spans both FIRs' complaint windows

transactions.note: Weekly payout, tagged to the FIR 9004 front company
Same destination account as TX-1, different front company - the fusion link

contradiction.suggestedNextQuestion: Ask Tarun why 'unrelated' QuickCash and RapidFin payouts both settle into the same Kotak xx3390 account, and why his weekly ops calls to that account's holder don't stop between the two companies' operating windows.

cases.title: Bengaluru Turf Assault
cases.summary: A street-gang turf dispute erupts into a multi-person assault outside a college, with dense CCTV coverage typical of an urban setting and conflicting accounts of who struck first.

firs.BriefFacts: Group clash outside a college gate involving 6+ young men, resulting in 2 hospitalized with head injuries; both sides claim the other started it.

calls.note: 2 hours before, the other side's coordination

cctv.personOrVehicle: Both groups converging from opposite directions

cctv.cameraLocation: College main gate camera, wider angle
cctv.personOrVehicle: Bharath Gowda throwing the first visible strike
cctv.note: Directly contradicts Zaid's group's claim that Bharath's side struck second

witnessStatements.statementText: Bharath's group attacked us first without provocation. We only defended ourselves.
Zaid's group blocked our path and started it. We acted in self-defense.

timeline.description: First visible strike, by Bharath - contradicts Zaid's self-defense claim being about who struck first

contradiction.suggestedNextQuestion: Show Bharath the wide-angle CCTV timestamped 17:31 and ask him to reconcile it with his statement that Zaid's group struck first - and ask why his side's coordination call (2 hours prior) precedes Zaid's side's (40 min prior) by so much, if this was a reactive, unplanned encounter.
